payload.prompt: The payment from Blueshore Ltd (org no. 989902121) for the invoice "Software License" (39700 NOK excl. VAT) was returned by the bank. Reverse the payment so the invoice shows the outstanding amount again.

payload.goal: Reverse the returned bank payment from Blueshore Ltd so that invoice 'Software License' (39700 NOK excl. VAT) is restored to outstanding/unpaid status.
success_checks: Payment voucher for Blueshore Ltd is successfully reversed
Invoice 'Software License' shows outstanding balance of 39700 NOK excl. VAT (49625 NOK incl. 25% VAT)
Customer ledger for Blueshore Ltd reflects the open receivable
No duplicate or orphaned vouchers remain after reversal
risk_notes: VAT rate not explicitly stated; defaulting to 25% (standard Norwegian MVA) — verify if a different rate applies
The original payment voucher ID/reference is not provided; must be located in the system before reversal
Invoice number or internal ID for 'Software License' is not specified; must be looked up by customer and amount
If the payment was already reconciled against a bank statement, bank reconciliation may need to be undone first
Sandbox is empty — full prerequisite chain (bank account, customer, product, order, invoice, payment) must be established before reversal can be executed
Org no. 989902121 should be validated against Brønnøysund register
payload.suggested_first_action: Search for customer Blueshore Ltd (org no. 989902121) in the customer registry to confirm existence, then locate the original payment voucher linked to invoice 'Software License'.
ordered_steps: 1. POST /ledger/account or verify bank account is configured in chart of accounts
2. POST /customer — create Blueshore Ltd with org no. 989902121 if not existing
3. POST /product — create 'Software License' product at 39700 NOK excl. VAT, VAT 25%
4. POST /order — create sales order for Blueshore Ltd
5. POST /order/{id}/orderline — add 'Software License' line item (qty 1, 39700 NOK excl. VAT)
7. POST /ledger/voucher — register the original payment against the invoice
8. GET /ledger/voucher — locate the payment voucher linked to 'Software License' invoice for Blueshore Ltd
9. PUT /ledger/voucher/{voucherId}/reverse — reverse the payment voucher to restore invoice to outstanding
10. GET /invoice/{id} — verify invoice status returns to 'UNPAID' with outstanding amount 39700 NOK excl. VAT
11. GET /customer/ledger — confirm open receivable is restored for Blueshore Ltd

planned_endpoints.summary: Find vouchers corresponding with sent data.
Reverses the voucher, and returns the reversed voucher. Supports reversing most voucher types, except salary transactions.
Create customer. Related customer addresses may also be created.
Add new voucher. IMPORTANT: Also creates postings. Only the gross amounts will be used. Amounts should be rounded to 2 decimals.

rules: REQUIRES dateFrom and dateTo as query params. Without them you get 422.
Example: params={"dateFrom": "2026-01-01", "dateTo": "2026-12-31"}
Use a broad date range. For year-end: dateFrom=YYYY-01-01, dateTo=YYYY-12-31.
Optional filters: number, description.
These are QUERY PARAMS via the params field — NOT json_body.
Method is PUT, not POST.
date is a QUERY PARAMETER: PUT /ledger/voucher/{id}/:reverse?date=YYYY-MM-DD
Do NOT send date in the request body.
When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
Do NOT send isCustomer (it's readOnly and auto-set).
For addresses, use postalAddress={addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161}} for Norway.
ALWAYS search first if product_number is provided: GET /product?number=<number> — sandbox pre-seeds products.
Only POST /product if GET returns 0 results.
Use 'number' field for the product number (NOT productNumber).
priceExcludingVat sets the base price. Also set vatType={"id": 3|5|6}.
Requires customer={"id": customer_id}.
Set orderDate and deliveryDate (use today_iso from execution_brief).
ALWAYS set BOTH amountGross AND amountGrossCurrency to the SAME value on every posting.
Do NOT include postings with row=0 — row 0 is system-generated and will cause a 422.
POSTING BALANCE RULES (which determines single-leg vs manual-leg):
vatType != 0 (e.g. id=3 for 25%): include ONLY the debit posting with GROSS amount. Tripletex auto-generates VAT + credit.
vatType == 0 (exempt): include BOTH debit AND credit postings manually. They must sum to 0.
If you get 422 'postings don't sum to 0': you used vatType=0 but only one posting. Either add the credit posting manually OR change to the correct vatType (e.g. 3 for 25%).
NEVER default to vatType=0 for standard purchases — use vatType=3 (25%) unless explicitly VAT-exempt.
For supplier invoices, set supplier={"id": supplier_id} on the debit posting.
For salary/payroll vouchers, set employee={"id": employee_id} on each posting.
Resolve account numbers: GET /ledger/account with params={"number": XXXX}, then use account={"id": resolved_id}.

payload.headline: Payment reversal mostly correct but one scoring check failed, likely invoice amount or VAT issue
what_went_wrong: Check 3 failed — likely the invoice amount, VAT type, or payment amount was incorrect. The agent used VAT type id=3 (25%) but the correct VAT type for this context may differ.
The agent created a new invoice/order chain instead of finding a pre-existing invoice for 'Software License' — the task says 'the payment was returned', implying the invoice already existed.

The enforcer flagged a potential duplicate product issue but was overridden; the sandbox may have had pre-seeded data that the agent missed by not checking GET /invoice or GET /customer/invoices first.
what_worked: Successfully reversed the payment voucher using PUT /ledger/voucher/:reverse, passing checks 1 and 2.
Clean execution with 0 error responses across 11 API calls.
what_to_try_next: Before creating any entities, search for existing invoices with GET /invoice?customerId=108506694 to find the pre-existing 'Software License' invoice rather than recreating the full chain.
If the invoice already exists, skip product/order/invoice creation entirely — just find the payment voucher via GET /ledger/voucher and reverse it directly, reducing calls from 11 to ~3.
Verify the correct VAT type by calling GET /vat/type before assuming id=3 is 25% — a wrong VAT type could cause the amount check to fail.
unnecessary_calls: POST /product — unnecessary if the invoice already existed in the sandbox; should check GET /invoice first
POST /order — unnecessary if pre-existing invoice found; entire order creation chain could be skipped
PUT /ledger/account/485403052 — configuring bank account may be unnecessary if payment type already works without it
